name: Language Arts
topics: Nouns · Verbs · Adjectives · Simple past · Plurals · Punctuation · Synonyms & antonyms

licoes.titulo: Nouns: people, places, animals and things
licoes.texto: A noun names a person, a place, an animal or a thing. (Substantivo)
pontos: Common nouns: any one of a kind: girl, city, dog.
Proper nouns: a special name. They start with a capital letter: Liz, London, Brazil.
licoes.fala: My name is a proper noun, so it starts with a capital L!

licoes.texto: A verb tells what someone or something does or is. (Verbo)
pontos: Action verbs: run, jump, read, swim.
Being verbs: am, is, are, was, were.
Theo kicks the ball. “Kicks” is the verb.
licoes.fala: I run, I jump, I kick! Verbs are the action of the sentence.

licoes.texto: An adjective describes a noun: color, size, shape or feeling. (Adjetivo)
pontos: a beautiful garden, a small cat, a happy day.
To compare two things, add -er: tall → taller.
To compare three or more, add -est: tall → tallest.
Short words ending in consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: big → bigger → biggest.
licoes.fala: An elephant is bigger than a mouse, and a blue whale is the biggest of all!

licoes.titulo: Simple past: things that already happened
licoes.texto: We use the simple past to talk about finished actions: yesterday, last week, in 2020.
pontos: Regular verbs: add -ed: play → played. Ending in consonant + y: study → studied.
Irregular verbs change: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had, run → ran.
Was with I, he, she, it. Were with you, we, they: The weather was sunny. We were happy.
licoes.fala: Yesterday I went to the park and played with my friends. Went and played are in the past!

licoes.texto: Most nouns just add -s: cat → cats. But watch out:
pontos: Ending in s, x, ch, sh: add -es: box → boxes, bus → buses.
Consonant + y: change to -ies: baby → babies.
Irregular: child → children, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice.
licoes.fala: One mouse, two mice! English plurals can be tricky.

licoes.texto: Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with an end mark.
pontos: . period: a telling sentence. ? question mark: a question. ! exclamation mark: strong feeling.
In English, these always start with a capital: names, the word I, days (Monday) and months (October).
Command: tells someone to do something: Close the door, please.
licoes.fala: In Portuguese we write “outubro”, but in English it is always “October” with a capital O!

licoes.texto: Synonyms have similar meanings. Antonyms have opposite meanings.
pontos: Synonyms: happy = glad, big = large, fast = quick.
Antonyms: hot × cold, early × late, full × empty.
Conjunctions join ideas: and (add), but (contrast), because (reason), so (result), or (choice).
licoes.fala: I was glad, which means happy, because we won the game!

questions.fb: Mia is a special name, so it is a proper noun and starts with a capital letter. (Substantivo próprio.)
“Cat” is an animal, so it is a noun. “Happy” is an adjective and “sleeps” is a verb.
“Kicks” is the action Theo does, so it is the verb.
“Swim” is something you do. Blue is an adjective, table is a noun.

questions.q: Find the adjective: Joana has a beautiful garden.
questions.fb: “Beautiful” describes the garden, so it is an adjective.

questions.q: Complete: An elephant is ___ than a mouse.
questions.fb: To compare two things we use -er: bigger. (Big doubles the g: big → bigger.)

questions.q: Complete: Gael is the ___ runner in the class.
questions.fb: Comparing one with the whole group, we use -est: the fastest.
Play is a regular verb: just add -ed → played.
Go is irregular: go → went. Example: We went to the zoo.
“Yesterday” tells us it is the past. Eat is irregular: eat → ate.

questions.q: Complete: Caio and Manu ___ at the museum last Saturday.
questions.fb: Caio and Manu = they. With they, we use were.
The weather = it. With it, the past is was.
Consonant + y: change y to i and add -ed → studied.
Words ending in x add -es: boxes.
Child is irregular: one child, two children.
Consonant + y: change to -ies → babies.
Tooth is irregular: one tooth, many teeth (like foot → feet).

opts: on monday, liz went to school.
On Monday, Liz went to school.
On monday, Liz went to School.
on Monday, liz went to school.
questions.fb: Capital letters: the first word, names (Liz) and days of the week (Monday).

questions.q: Which word must always start with a capital letter in English?
questions.fb: Months and days always start with a capital in English: October, Monday.

questions.q: Which end mark goes here? Where is my backpack
questions.fb: It is a question, so it ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Wow, we won the game — which end mark shows strong feeling?
questions.fb: The exclamation mark shows strong feeling: Wow, we won the game!

questions.q: Close the door, please. What kind of sentence is this?
questions.fb: It tells someone to do something, so it is a command.
Synonyms mean almost the same: happy = glad. Sad is the antonym.
Antonyms are opposites: hot × cold.
Early × late. (Cedo × tarde.)

questions.q: Complete: Mia stayed home ___ it was raining a lot.
questions.fb: “Because” gives the reason: Mia stayed home because it was raining.

questions.q: Complete: I like apples, ___ I don't like bananas.
questions.fb: “But” shows a contrast between two ideas.

questions.q: Read: Liz has a small garden. Every morning, Liz waters the tomatoes and the sunflowers. The sunflowers are taller than Liz! What does Liz do every morning?
questions.fb: The text says: “Every morning, Liz waters the tomatoes and the sunflowers.”

questions.q: Read again: The sunflowers are taller than Liz! Which is taller?
questions.fb: “Taller than Liz” means the sunflowers are taller.
Contraction: do + not = don't. The apostrophe (') takes the place of the letter o.
